- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-0.50) and model forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 3–7% to offset negative sentiment bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.  
- When supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates upside; add 1–3% to forecast mean for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → -0.50 → 0.00), model may misread trend; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check if recent events (especially auctions) are underrepresented; adjust forecast by +1–3% if supply net is negative and events are bullish.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and model forecast is trending, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence in “no sentiment” periods.
